note: Bake-off arms. Secret values NEVER live here: secretEnv maps a backend config key to the NAME of an environment variable the runner reads at boot. Everything under commonEnv is a bench-only value for a throwaway local API (documented in README.md and the report), never a production setting.
modelIdsCheckedLive: 2026-10-03: all five chat model ids answered with the adapter's own request shape (orchestrator check before this build). Re-check on the run day.

vertex.note: Availability is decided at run time from whether these NAMES are set, never here. A Vertex arm without them is refused unless --vertex-fallback-ai-studio is passed; that choice is the owner's and is recorded in arm-run.json and in the report. Arm 2 is the first live Vertex call ever (N15): a 400 on the shared snake_case body stops that arm, and the adapter fix is a separate, approved change. Every probe is adult-written synthetic text already in the repo; no child data reaches either backend. The production flip to Vertex still needs Google's under-18 confirmation (C035).

secretEnvNote: Gemini__Vertex__* are passed only to an arm that runs on Vertex. The backend reads GEMINI_API_KEY itself (secretEnvPassThrough); the calibration call uses it for every Gemini arm, Vertex arms included.

commonEnvWhy.Devices__AllowOpenRegistration: the runner and the benchmarks register a fresh toy per unit with no provisioning secret
commonEnvWhy.RateLimiting__Auth__PermitLimit: one register + claim per unit; the production 10-per-60s auth bucket would 429 the run
commonEnvWhy.RateLimiting__Chat__PermitLimit: calls are strictly sequential; the cap is lifted so a slow arm is never throttled into canned replies
commonEnvWhy.OpenAI__DailyCostCap__Default: the $0.25/toy/day cap would inject the canned pause line mid-persona and poison the comparison
commonEnvWhy.Backup__Database__Enabled: no snapshot of a throwaway DB
commonEnvWhy.Alerts__WebhookUrl: never page anyone from a bench

spend.note: The guard prices a call with the calibration's measured tokens (reasoning/thinking included) once an arm has one, and arms.json's assumptions until then. Its figure is the larger of that estimate and the arm DB's DeviceUsageDays meter, which under-counts the chat path (question-only EstimateChatCostUsd). Every unit is checked against the arm budget, cumulativeStopUsd and hardCapUsd across EVERY runs folder in the ledger ($BAKEOFF_LEDGER, default <runs parent>/bakeoff-ledger.json). It is a guard, not the cap: the provider-side project budgets (OpenAI 'areg-bakeoff' $40, Google $60) are the hard cap and must be set before any live run.

estimate.note: Guard assumptions only, NOT measurements. The token-measurement step of the plan replaces them in the cost write-up.
estimate.sttSource: gpt-live-transcribe $0.017/min (docs/ai-landscape-2026-09.md); gpt-transcribe batch is not dearer as far as known, so this is the guard ceiling
estimate.benchmarkChatTurnsSource: prompts/scenarios.json turn counts at 2026-10-03; Story counts an opening + one continuation per prompt, Mode adds ~12 gate/claim scenario turns

defaultPassesWhy: The plan: 3 passes on the safety and persona sets (worst-of-3, majority-of-3); voice-latency and the benchmarks run once. An arm's own `passes` caps it.
